findings.evidence: Tensor.lean:136-137 vs 177-178; roadmap README.md:392-400 defines `fromG1G2` as producing the displayed `(M/(p·q))·g1·E₁ + (1/(M(p·q)))·g2·E₂` from two reals and says it 'should be named and shaped to match' `IsF1F2Decomposition`/`fromF1F2`; README.md:478 expects the 0.3 inversion applied to `fromG1G2 g K c₁ c₂` to return `c₁`, `c₂`, which holds only if those reals are g₁, g₂.
findings.fix: Fold the kinematic prefactors into `fromG1G2` so its two reals are the g₁, g₂ values (`fromG1G2 ε K g1 g2 = (√(M2)/(p·q) * g1) • E₁ + ((√(M2))⁻¹/(p·q) * g2) • E₂`), letting `IsG1G2Decomposition` read `W = fromG1G2 ε K (G.g1 (K.xBj g) (K.Q2 g)) (G.g2 …)`; or keep the plain combination under a coefficient-neutral name (e.g. `spinCombination`) and reserve `fromG1G2` for the prefactored constructor.
findings.issue: `fromG1G2 ε K c₁ c₂ = c₁ • E₁ + c₂ • E₂` takes the bare coefficients of E₁, E₂, not g₁ and g₂: `IsG1G2Decomposition` (177-178) must itself insert `√(K.M2 g)/g K.p K.q *` and `(√(K.M2 g))⁻¹/g K.p K.q *`. The name promises the structure functions, so `fromG1G2 ε K (G.g1 x Q2) (G.g2 x Q2)` silently yields a tensor off by `M/(p·q)` — unlike `fromF1F2 g K F1 F2` (Tensors/Basic.lean:620), whose arguments are the structure functions and which `IsF1F2Decomposition g K W F1 F2` consumes unchanged. Same name applies to `fromG1G2_apply` (140), `fromG1G2_isAlt` (146), `tensorAssumptions_fromG1G2` (152), `fromG1G2_conserved_left/right` (157, 162) and `fromG1G2_isDecomposition` (182), which for this reason has to spell the prefactors out instead of being the characterising lemma `fromF1F2_isDecomposition` (Tensors/Basic.lean:632) is.

findings.evidence: Tensor.lean:213-215 statement; Tensor.lean:32-33 'exhibits Minkowski kinematics on ℝ⁴ on which E₁ and E₂ are linearly independent'; contrast Tensors/Basic.lean:312-314.
findings.fix: Name it for the conclusion it proves, e.g. `exists_spinStructure_linearIndependent` (optionally restating as `LinearIndependent ℝ ![spinStructureOne ε K, spinStructureTwo ε K]`), or at minimum `exists_fromG1G2_ne_zero_of_coeff_ne_zero`.
findings.issue: `exists_fromG1G2_ne_zero` names the conclusion of the much weaker `exists_lMuNuOdd_ne_zero` pattern (Tensors/Basic.lean:312, `∃ ε K, lMuNuOdd ε K ≠ 0`), while the statement is the linear independence of E₁ and E₂ (`∀ c₁ c₂, (c₁ ≠ 0 ∨ c₂ ≠ 0) → fromG1G2 ε K c₁ c₂ ≠ 0`), which is what the docstring and module header advertise as the non-degeneracy witness.

summary: `fromG1G2` is named for g₁/g₂ but takes the raw coefficients of E₁/E₂, so `fromG1G2 ε K (G.g1 x Q2) (G.g2 x Q2)` is not the decomposed tensor; `exists_fromG1G2_ne_zero` names a weaker conclusion than it proves. Everything else matches the `fromF1F2`/`lMuNuOdd` precedent and the roadmap names.
